siteOverview.title: Connecting the work across Africa
siteOverview.lead: Possibilities Africa walks with local pastors in seven countries. Use the tabs below to see what each part of this site is about — then open a section when you want to go deeper.

tabs.label: Who we are
tabs.imageAlt: Pastor speaking with a rural congregation in East Africa
tabs.title: Pastors and churches leading change
tabs.lead: We exist so rural families grow in faith and in everyday life — food, water, health, and work. Local pastors carry the vision. Possibilities Africa walks beside them.
bullets: Rural churches are already in the community — we build on what is there.
Change lasts when local people own it, not when outsiders run it.
Faith and daily life belong together — spiritual growth and practical help side by side.

highlights.title: Inclusive
highlights.text: Women, youth, and households are part of the change.

highlights.title: Resilient
highlights.text: Skills and assets that last beyond one project.

tabs.label: Where we work
tabs.imageAlt: Aerial view of villages across the East and Southern Africa landscape
tabs.title: Seven countries, one path on the ground
tabs.lead: The work runs in Kenya, Malawi, Ethiopia, Zambia, Tanzania, Rwanda, and Burundi. On this site you can open a country and drill down to a nearby group of communities, then one community.
bullets: Start on the map of Africa — pick a country to see pastors and communities there.
Each country has catchment areas: 3–5 neighbouring communities that share pastor leaders.
Each community walks a two-year journey — you can follow one place from start to finish.

tabs.label: What we do
tabs.imageAlt: Pastor and community members planning a local project together
tabs.title: A clear two-year path with pastors
tabs.lead: Every community moves through five stages over about two years — from first awareness to helping neighbours copy the work. Pastors grow through training, Shalom groups meet, and local projects begin.
bullets: Pastors lead — trained and supported through awareness, ability, and action.
Shalom groups of 30–50 leaders in each community deepen discipleship and local initiative.
Communities plan their own work: water, farming, health, jobs, and more.

highlights.title: Two-year journey
highlights.text: Five stages from first steps to multiplication.

highlights.title: Local projects
highlights.text: Church-led plans owned by the community.

tabs.label: Our results
tabs.imageAlt: Community leaders reviewing progress and results together
tabs.title: Simple numbers beside the stories
tabs.lead: We track communities, homes, pastors, and projects across the network. Results pages show what is improving — water, farming, health, schools, and leadership — without replacing the people behind the figures.
bullets: See how many communities are on the journey and how homes are reached.
Check what is working in water, farming, health, and jobs — in plain words.
Read what is changing over time — where the work began and what may come next.
